comment.narrative: During the MTR mission, MEF and ANDA clarified progress. The pilots to be developed are: Atlantic Seaweed Culture Demonstration Project in Souss Massa Region; and Diversifying aquaculture production through a pilot project for shrimp in drylands.

ANDA reported that 1 pilot farm on shrimp farming has been established. Once the project completion report is prepared, the indicator will be marked as completed. ANDA is also preparing the second pilot farm.

title.narrative: Indicator 12: People consulted for the planning and management of MPAs

comment.narrative: As per Law 22-07 on Protected Areas, DPM concluded the public consultation for the MPA in Agadir. The stakeholder engagement process was initiated in Larache and C3F. The public consultation for Larache was held on February 27, 2024. 84 people took part, including 23% women and 32% young people. The task team will assess the progress during the next mission.

title.narrative: Indicator 9: People reached by international and national coastal tourism advertisement campaigns

comment.narrative: The final target for this indicator was achieved. Thanks to the success of the campaigns and events such as the 2024 World Cup, the campaign had a good reach, exceeding the final target set for the program. The PMU and the ONMT should consider increasing the target as part of the restructuring. The ONMT is invited to analyze the impact of the communication campaign, such as the increase in the number of overnight stays. The PMU and the ONMT must include the formula for calculating the number of people affected in the MOP.

title.narrative: Indicator 12: People consulted for the planning and management of MPAs

comment.narrative: The Agadir MPA public consultation has concluded as part of the process for declaring the area protected. The consultation process has begun at Cap Toir Fourche and Larache. The marine area management planning (MSP) including consultations, under the Grant is to be launched as soon as possible for the C3F and Larache MPAs. â€¢ Public consultation Agadir : 941 (871 men, 70 women). â€¢ Public consultation for Larache: 84 (39 men, 19 women, 26 young people). â€¢ Public consultation for Nador: 60 (41 men, 9 women, 10 young people).

title.narrative: Indicator 1: Progress in the implementation of blue economy communication campaigns

comment.narrative: The communication plan has been drawn up by DDD. Based on the activities set by the communication plan, 25% has been achieved. DDD shared the final communication plan with the PIU. The PIU needs to collect evidence showing the progress against the plan.

title.narrative: Indicator 1: Progress in the implementation of blue economy communication campaigns

comment.narrative: The communication plan to structure BE awareness-rasing and information dissemination has been drawn up by DDD. Based on the activities set by the communication plan, 25% has been achieved. DDD shared the final communication plan with the PIU. DDD needs to communicate progress made in 2024 to UGP, along with evidence of this progress, such as communication materials. DDD to share communication materials with ONMT with a view to possible cooperation.

title.narrative: Indicator 9: People reached by international and national coastal tourism advertisement campaigns

comment.narrative: Progress is on track and has exceeded annual targets. Until the end of 2023, the campaigns reached 220,000,000 people and this result was verified and EUR 1,802,800 were disbursed against DLI 5 in January 2024.During the last mission, ONMT reported that the campaigns reached additional 665,227 people. The task team will assess the progress during the next mission.

title.narrative: Indicator 8: Tourism areas in Aghroud equipped with basic utility services in accordance with NDC

baseline.value: No area is equipped. No SDR exists for Aghroud.

comment.narrative: The Aghroud SDR is not operational and no areas have been equipped. It has been confirmed that this activity is not in line with the regional government. Official request to restructure activity received February 5, 2025. The PIU will finalize the identification of alternative projects to be included in the restructuring.

actual.value: No area is equipped. SDR for Aghroud is established

title.narrative: Indicator 8: Tourism areas in Aghroud equipped with basic utility services in accordance with NDC

baseline.value: No area is equipped. No SDR exists for Aghroud.

comment.narrative: This activity has been re-programmed by the regional government and that will have implications in the SMIT programming and budgeting under the PforR. In response to current regional strategic priorities, activities aligned with the Blue Agadir initiative have been proposed to be part of the PforR. During the last mission, the task team visited the sites of the activities proposed by the regional authorities to know its objectives and the environmental and social characteristics of its location as well as indicate what information might be necessary to carry out a more detailed analysis. This set of intervention respond to the need to consolidate the blue touristic offer and services around Agadir, before expanding to the development of new areas. The PIU plans to bring the reprogramming of this activity for the attention and guidance by the CIDEB. Due to the delay with the organization of the first meeting, the MEF has not communicated a formal request to the Bank.

actual.value: No area is equipped. SDR for Aghroud is established

title.narrative: Indicator 3: A data portal on the BE is operational to enable evidence-based decision-making and implement the BE strategy in line with NDC

comment.narrative: The PIU launched the BE portal (https://blueeconomy.gov.ma/). The enhancement of the portal was supported by the IPF grant. The PIU is advised to prepare a plan to continue developing the portal, especially to integrate sector data to support decision-making on the blue economy. MEF shall ensure that resources are allocated to the ongoing maintenance of the portal. The PMU could use the portal for the BE strategy process, including public consultation.

title.narrative: Indicator 1: Strengthened institutional frameworks to guide collaborative implementation of the BE strategy in targeted areas

comment.narrative:
At the Council of Government held on December 21, 2023, the Head of Government invited the Ministry of Economy and Finance to prepare a meeting of the Inter-ministerial Commission for the Development of the Blue Economy (CIDEB). The first meeting of the CIDEB was planned for October 2024 but it was postponed due to the changes in the government.
The progress on the Score stands at 2.7: The commission was set up by circular N3/2023 (criterion 1); the blue economy portal was created (criterion 2); the citizen was informed by news published on the MEF website and the BE portal (criterion 12); at least one coordination meeting was organized for each of the pilot regions (criterion 14).

title.narrative: Indicator 1: Strengthened institutional frameworks to guide collaborative implementation of the BE strategy in targeted areas

comment.narrative: The progress on the Score stands at 2.7: The commission was set up by circular N3/2023 (criterion 1); the blue economy portal was created (criterion 2); the citizen was informed by news published on the MEF website and the BE portal (criterion 12); The commission was set up by the circular (criterion 1); The first meeting of the Technical Committee was held during the fourth supervision mission on 29 February 2024. (criterion 11); The citizen was informed by news published on the MEF website (criterion 12). Coordination meetings were held in the TTA and SM regions (criterion 14). Head of Goverment authorized MEF to chair the interministerial commission. The first meeting is scheduled for March 2025. The draft workplan will be submitted to the first meeting.

title.narrative: Indicator 2: Government officials at the national and regional levels certified in capacity building to promote the BE in alignment with NDC

comment.narrative: No training program is in place yet. The Bank, with BETF resources, has supported the PIU to develop capacity on collaborative leadership, social norms, problem definition, solution design and research methods. The PIU is procuring a service provider to support the development of a capacity building program under the IPF grant. The PIU plans to leverage the cooperation agreement with the Mohammed VI University of Health Sciences to develop the certification program. PMU to finalize TOR for technical assistance to develop executive program under the grant.

title.narrative: Indicator 2: Government officials at the national and regional levels certified in capacity building to promote the BE in alignment with NDC

comment.narrative: The Bank, with BETF resources, has supported the PIU to develop capacity on collaborative leadership, social norms, problem definition, solution design and research methods.The PIU is procuring a service provider to support the development of a capacity building program under the small IPF grant. The PIU plans to leverage the cooperation agreement with the Mohammed VI University of Health Sciences to develop the certification program. The PIU has been requested to accelerate the implementation of this activity and maximize the use of the resources.

title.narrative: Indicator 3: Aquaculture farms established and operational in targeted areas

comment.narrative: ANDA is continuing preparatory work including the procurement of equipment. Five farms are expected to be established by December 2024.

title.narrative: Indicator 2: Tourism MSMEs that are established or transformed in line with NDC pathway for development through SMITâ€™s incubator program in targeted areas

comment.narrative: SDR Souss-Massa is operational. In the Souss Massa region, 99 MSMEs have been selected to participate in the creation or transformation process. These SMEs are currently participating in the incubation program and receiving training. A call of proposals for the second round of the incubation program was launched in February 2024. The SDR TPME coastal Guelmin and SDR Tangier-Tetouan-Al Hoceima have been created. The team will review the progress during the next mission.

title.narrative: Indicator 3: Aquaculture farms established and operational in targeted areas

comment.narrative: ANDA is continuing preparatory work including the procurement of equipment. Five farms, originally expected to be established by December 2024 will be in place by 2025 (according to ANDA, 1 already installed (Vitamin Sea)). The PIU and ANDA will work together to launch the verification as soon as these farms are established. During MTR, MEF and ANDA clarified that targets under PDO indicator 3 (14 farms) are not being double-counted under Intermediate Indicator 10 (2 pilot farms).

title.narrative: Indicator 2: Tourism MSMEs that are established or transformed in line with NDC pathway for development through SMITâ€™s incubator program in targeted areas

comment.narrative:
109 TPMEs have been transformed or created in the region Souss Massa,19 of which are run by women. The PMU will closely monitor the SMIT work plan to ensure its implementation.
Mobilizing women entrepreneurs remains a major challenge. There is a risk of not achieving the final target and the target of 40% participation of women.
In Guelmin, the first call for projects was launched on 12 February 2025.
At the Tangier region, the recruitment of the director of the SDR TPME failed three times, which led to a delay in the launch of the incubation program. As a result, SDR Tangier has not yet started its activities.

title.narrative: Indicator 11: People are professionally trained for a climate-resilient BE and ready to support NDC

comment.narrative: The progress on this indicator is below the annual target. The PIU has been requested to work with implementing partners, especially with ANDA to ensure that the final target will be met. In 2023, DPDPM trained 15 people (of which 12 were women) and DDD trained 50 people (of which 25 were women). ANDA did not conduct any training. In 2024, DDD carried out a simulation exercise. DDD will communicate the progress to PIU.

title.narrative: Indicator 11: People are professionally trained for a climate-resilient BE and ready to support NDC

comment.narrative:
Activities are slightly delayed. This ISR corrects the previously misreported status of this indicator. â€¢ In 2022, 219 people reported as trained. DPDPM reported 16 people (of which 8 were women); ANDA reported 50 people; DDD reported 153. â€¢ In 2023, DPDPM reported 15 people trained (of which 12 were women) and DDD reported 67 people (of which 22 were women). ANDA did not carry out any training. â€¢ In 2024, DPDPM reported 27 additional professionals; DDD reported 170 additional professionals.; ANDA did not carry out any training.
PIU will work with ANDA to prepare a work plan for the training so that ANDA's backlog can be cleared and the final objective achieved. The PIU must set up a mechanism to consolidate partner reports.This indicator needs to be fully reviewd. During the restructuring the team will confirm with UGP the final numbers of ANDA.

title.narrative: Indicator 7: Shellfish production areas in targeted areas covered by the health monitoring program

comment.narrative: The indicator is on track. As of this interim ISR, the PIU reported the assessment of 14,800ha in 2024. The technical report for 2024 will be prepared early 2025.

title.narrative: Indicator 7: Shellfish production areas in targeted areas covered by the health monitoring program

comment.narrative: The final target for this indicator was reached. 17,200 ha of production area were classified. The extension of one zone and two new zones were classified in 2024, exceeding the final target. INRH to share the technical report with the PMU by March 2025.

title.narrative: Indicator 6: Fish stocks in targeted areas are assessed

comment.narrative: Progress is on track. 15 stocks were evaluated in December 2024.

title.narrative: Indicator 6: Fish stocks in targeted areas are assessed

comment.narrative: The progress is on track. The assessment of 14 stocks in 2023 was verified in October 2024. As of this interim ISR, the PIU reported the assessment of 15 fish stocks in 2024.

title.narrative: Indicator 5: Beaches in targeted areas covered by environmental monitoring programs

comment.narrative: The indicator is on track. The beach monitoring campaigns in 2023 covering 182 beaches were verified in October 2024. DDD reported the completion of the beach monitoring campaigns in 2024. The team will assess the progress during the next mission.

title.narrative: Indicator 5: Beaches in targeted areas covered by environmental monitoring programs

comment.narrative: This activity has been slightly delayed due to the limited budgets allocated to the DDD and the rising costs of laboratory analyses. By 2024, 184 beaches will have been assessed. By 2025, 200 beaches should have been assessed. DDD to hold bilateral talks with MEF; Task Team and MEF to review proposed changes to the verification protocol.

title.narrative: Indicator 13: Sites improved in accordance with biodiversity conservation management plans

comment.narrative: ANEF has implemented activities in Souss Masa National Park, Al Hoceima National Park and Jbel Moussa. Due to ANEF's institutional change from DEF, no progress has been made on this activity in 2023. In 2024, ANEF plans to cover 5 conservatio nareas (Souss Massa National Park; Al-Hoceima National Park; Jbel Moussa; KhAnifiss National Park and Tamri). Copies of management plans need to be provided to the Bank.

title.narrative: Indicator 13: Sites improved in accordance with biodiversity conservation management plans

comment.narrative: This indicator is on track. 5 sites were managed in 2024. ANEF has made up for the delay caused by institutional change.

title.narrative: Indicator 4: Marine and coastal areas under climate-resilient and sustainable integrated management in targeted areas

comment.narrative: This indicator is reporting progress but there is a risk of not meeting the final target within the project timeframe due to the accumulated delay. As of the date if this ISR, 7,405ha of coastal forests have been restored. The work on the fixation of coastal dune for 60ha has started and is ongoing. Regarding the MPAs, the public consultation process for the MPA Agadir has been finalized. The preparatory work for the MPA in Cape Trois Fourches and MPA in Larache are ongoing, with consultations processes. The preparation of management plans need to be accelerated for all three MPAs. The PIU has been requested to optimize the support of the small IPF associated the establishement of MPAs and the prepration of the management plans.

title.narrative: Indicator 4: Marine and coastal areas under climate-resilient and sustainable integrated management in targeted areas

comment.narrative: The overall progress of the indicator has been delayed, mainly due to the lengthy legal proceedings for declaring AMPs. The delay linked to the reforestation and fixation of coastal dunes has been resolved and work is now progressing according to plan.

title.narrative: Indicator 4: Coastal areas assessed by remote sensing to monitor shoreline changes in targeted areas and summarized in monitoring reports

comment.narrative: The progress is reported to be on track. The assessment of 1,295,000ha (DLI3.a) was verified and EUR 2,529,060 were disbursed in January 2024. DPDPM reported that it assessed cumulative 1,690,000 ha of coastal area assessed during 2023. However, IGF pointed out issues with evaluation methodologies. The PIU and DPDPM are reexamining the evaluation methodology for the assessment conducted in 2023. In moving forward, the PIU is advised to use the technical assistance under the IPF grant to establish the methodology guideline and subsequently update the MOP.

title.narrative: Indicator 4: Coastal areas assessed by remote sensing to monitor shoreline changes in targeted areas and summarized in monitoring reports

comment.narrative: This activity is well underway. 610,000 ha have been assessed for 2022-2023. In 2023-2024, 395,000 ha have been assessed. In 2024-2025, 500,000 ha of images to be acquired. A total of 1,000,000 ha will be assessed in 2024-2025. The annual target for year 3 is on track.
